title: Latency-prioritized padding slicer with KV-prefetch cohorter
author: Noah Kim
release_notes: Introduce latency-prioritized padding slicer and KV-prefetch cohorter to reduce p99 tail latency and padding waste for heterogeneous sequence-length workloads. Feature behind runtime flag. No API changes.

d4e5f6: add KV-prefetch cohorter and TTL controls; integrate with cache manager

description:
Motivation: Heterogeneous sequence-length workloads create a tail-latency / padding tradeoff. Existing bucketing reduces padding but can increase scheduling overhead and miss kernel-fitting opportunities for hardware-aligned tile sizes. This PR introduces two complementary runtime heuristics: a latency-prioritized padding slicer and a KV-prefetch cohorter. Goals: reduce p99 generation latency for mixed-length traffic, lower average padding tokens (unit cost), and improve kernel utilization for common GPU tile sizes without changing public APIs.

Summary of changes: the padding slicer dynamically partitions incoming requests into cohorts using a stride-aware alignment strategy. Requests are mapped into alignment buckets based on sequence-length modulus against kernel-friendly stride sizes (configurable per-device). For cohorts where padding overhead dominates latency (many short sequences batched with a few long ones), the slicer opportunistically slices long sequences into aligned sub-requests for scheduling purposes only; semantics are preserved because slicing is local to the batch composition stage and recomposition happens before token emission. The KV-prefetch cohorter detects likely shared-prefix patterns (common in few-shot or template-driven workloads) and issues a low-cost asynchronous prefill of KV cache for cohorts to avoid repeated expensive prefill during the critical tail window. The runtime selects kernels per-cohort using a lightweight cost model that considers sequence-length distribution, expected padding, and kernel tile fit.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on an A100 cluster with mixed workloads (10k samples: 70% short <64, 20% mid 64-512, 10% long >512) show: median token latency ~3% improvement, p95 ~9% improvement, p99 ~15% improvement, and end-to-end padding token reduction ~10% in aggregate when feature flag enabled. Perf harness and scripts included for reproducibility (benchmarks/ci).

Compatibility and safety: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.padding_slicer.enabled and runtime.kv_prefetch.enabled. Default off for Dedicated customers until validated in canary. Slicing is disabled for requests that declare stateful generation semantics (chat streams with user-turn continuity) — we detect via request metadata. KV-prefetch respects KMS/HSM isolation (no secrets exfiltration) and uses existing cache TTL controls.

Testing and validation: added unit tests for alignment logic and TTL semantics, integration tests that exercise continuous batcher end-to-end, and a perf harness. Canary run executed in internal cluster; telemetry dashboards added (docs/ops/patch_notes) with new metrics: padding_savings_rate, kv_prefill_hits, cohort_miss_ratio.

Migration & operator notes: operators can tune stride sizes per-device and set maximum per-request slice count (default 3) to bound recomposition work. See docs/ops/patch_notes/latency_padding_slicer.md for runbook. No API surface changes.

Risk and rollback: initial canary flagged an off-by-one alignment that could increase padding for a narrow range of lengths (fixed in a follow-up commit). We added a kill-switch in the console to disable the feature per-cluster.

Related work: ENG-8912 (padding cost modeling), ENG-9034 (KV cache improvements).
